long_biography.plain_text:
Robert McNeil combined doctoral training in molecular biology, biochemistry and genetics with a conviction that scientific founders needed patient operating capital. He established Sanderling Ventures and built a model around seed and early-stage biomedical companies. Rather than remaining a distant financier, he worked with management teams, chaired portfolio companies and helped guide products through development. Investments included cardiovascular devices and therapeutics businesses that were later acquired by larger healthcare groups.

McNeil remained active in Sanderling's investment committee and company boards until shortly before his death. Away from biotechnology, he applied the same long-horizon approach to maritime preservation. Working with specialist shipwrights and historians, he led the reconstruction of a historic steam vessel and supported the restoration of a Gilded Age schooner. The projects combined archival research, traditional shipbuilding and modern engineering while retaining significant original machinery and interiors.
